newsitem.title: CANADA: Gaz Metropolitain to build gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Gaz Metropolitain to build gas pipeline.

text.p: Gaz Metropolitain said on Friday it plans to build a 220-kilometer natural gas pipeline between Lachenaie, Quebec, and the New Hampshire border at a cost of C$230 million.

The project to be conducted on behalf of TransQuebec & Maritimes Pipeline, a company in which Gaz Metropolitain and TransCanada PipeLines are equal partners, will supply the Portland Natural Gas Transmission System.
The pipeline will also bolster the natural gas distribution system in the Estrie region, in response to growing demand.

The Portland Natural Gas Transmission System, a project in which Gaz Metropolitain and TransCanada also have a stake, will carry Canadian natural gas to markets in New Hampshire, Maine and as far as Boston.
Construction is set to begin on December 1, 1997, and is scheduled to be in service on November 1, 1998. The proposal will be submitted to the National Energy Board.
The Regie du gaz naturel analyzed the project and handed down a decision. The regulatory body acknowledged the interest of such a project for Gaz Metropolitain customers.
Gaz Metropolitain said it would act as project manager.
